vulnerabilities.description: Command Injection vulnerability: User-controlled arguments are joined directly into shell command without proper escaping. While --body-file is used for body content, other arguments like command and subcommand are not validated. Attackers could inject shell metacharacters via these args.
Predictable Session ID Generation: Uses Date.now() which is easily predictable and can be enumerated. An attacker can guess valid session IDs to hijack sessions.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

vulnerabilities.description: Missing Authentication/Authorization: Task routing function does not validate who can submit or route tasks. No access control checks before processing tasks or coordinating agents.
Missing Input Validation: submitTask() accepts arbitrary task payloads without validation. No schema validation, type checking, or sanitization before processing.

Unencrypted Sensitive Data Storage: Memory data stored in plaintext JSON file at .claude-flow/data/memory.json. No encryption at rest. Sensitive campaign data, API keys, or credentials could be exposed.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

vulnerabilities.description: Plaintext Session Storage: Session data including context, metrics, and state stored unencrypted in .claude-flow/sessions/. No encryption or access controls.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

vulnerabilities.description: Unencrypted Memory Storage: Vector embeddings and memory entries stored in unencrypted maps. No access control on retrieve() or search() operations. Any agent can access any memory.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

vulnerabilities.description: Arbitrary Code Execution via Validation Functions: Validators accept arbitrary functions without sandboxing. Custom validation functions execute with full system access, allowing injection of malicious validators.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code

vulnerabilities.description: Potential XSS in Generated Content: Creative content (headlines, body, CTAs) generated without output sanitization. If displayed in web UI, could enable XSS attacks.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded Market Data: CPM and market data hardcoded in MARKET_DATA array. No validation that this data comes from trusted sources. Could be manipulated to produce false recommendations.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

vulnerabilities.description: No Rate Limiting: Task routing accepts unlimited concurrent tasks with no rate limiting. Could enable denial of service attacks.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

vulnerabilities.description: Weak Temporary File Name: Uses randomBytes(8).toString('hex') for temp file names. While better than predictable names, 16 hex chars could be enumerated in some scenarios. Should use OS-provided temp file creation.
Shell Command Execution with Pipes: Uses execSync with shell pipes (ps aux | grep). While hardcoded, represents risky pattern. Any future parameterization could introduce injection.
No Validation of Creative Content: Creative genome extraction and analysis accept arbitrary content without validation. Could process malicious payloads.
Missing Error Handling: JSON.parse errors silently caught but could hide data corruption or attacks. No logging of parse failures.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-390: Detection of Error Condition Without Action

recommendations: CRITICAL: Replace execSync in github-safe.js with shell escaping library (e.g., shellEscape) or use gh API directly without shell
CRITICAL: Generate session IDs using cryptographically secure random (crypto.randomUUID() or similar), minimum 32 bytes
CRITICAL: Implement authentication and authorization layer - validate user identity/permissions before routing tasks
HIGH: Implement comprehensive input validation on all agent task inputs - use schema validation (zod, joi)
HIGH: Encrypt all at-rest data - memory.json, session files, and in-memory state using AES-256
HIGH: Add audit logging for sensitive operations (task routing, memory access, session creation)
HIGH: Sandbox custom validation functions - use isolated worker threads or disable arbitrary function execution
MEDIUM: Add output sanitization for all generated content - escape HTML/special characters before display
MEDIUM: Implement rate limiting and circuit breakers on task routing and agent operations
MEDIUM: Validate and sign market data from external sources - implement cryptographic verification
MEDIUM: Add access control list (ACL) to memory operations - restrict which agents can access which memory types
MEDIUM: Use OS-provided temp file APIs instead of custom random naming
LOW: Add structured logging with error codes for all catch blocks
LOW: Document security assumptions and threat model for agent communication
LOW: Implement secrets detection - scan for API keys, passwords in generated content and logs
